title: fails on an id the triage does not cover, and names it
why: An id the triage has never seen passed over: OSV's new matches would never turn the weekly run red, which is the only notification there is.

title: fails on an open id past its due date, and not on the day it is due
why: The due date ignored: an open id stays green for ever, and the fix budget is a number nobody is held to.

title: never calls a network failure clean
why: A run that never reached OSV exits as a clean one: the week OSV is down is the week nothing is watched, and the run says all is well.

title: never calls a network failure clean
why: An HTTP error read as an answer: a 503 whose body happens to parse would be judged as OSV's word on the components.

title: never calls a network failure clean
why: A short answer taken whole: the queries OSV did not answer would read as components with no vulnerability.

title: reports a triaged id OSV no longer returns, without failing on it
why: A triaged id OSV has stopped returning goes unmentioned, so the triage keeps entries for fixes that have shipped and nobody is told to take them out.

title: takes an id triaged at another version as untriaged
why: A verdict read against one version kept after the pin moves: a not-reachable judged on 3.12.14 would stand for whatever the runtime becomes.

title: takes an id OSV now rates otherwise as untriaged
why: A re-rated id kept at its old rating: a medium raised to critical would keep its 60 days instead of 14.

find: if (!('due' in entry)) say('is open and has no "due" date')
title: refuses an open entry with no due date, and a closed one with one
why: An open entry with no due date accepted: it can never be overdue, so the budget never applies to it.

title: refuses a due date past the budget for its severity
why: A due date written past the budget accepted: a critical reachable id could be given a year.

title: builds one query per component from the pins, sharing one for two pins that ask the same
why: CPython asked about by its version rather than its tag: OSV's GIT records list tags, so the query matches nothing and the runtime's twenty-odd ids vanish from the watch.

title: refuses pins that name a component the watch does not read, or lack a field it reads
why: A component added to the pins without a query is let through, and the installers carry something the watch never asks about.

title: follows OSV's pages, and asks again only for the query that has another
why: Only OSV's first page read: a component with more ids than a page holds is judged on part of them.
